issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Lecture.getTotalNumberOfStudents(): the problem statement UML explicitly declares getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (problem_statement.md, UML line), but the solution implementation defines public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents() (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) and introduces a StudentCount wrapper type (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/StudentCount.java). This breaks the one-to-one mapping between the UML/specification and the provided solution: a student implementing the method to return an int (as instructed in the UML/hints) will produce a different signature than the solution and any tests that follow the solution's wrapper type. This inconsistency will confuse students about the expected return type and may cause test or compilation mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Two viable options: (A) Match the UML/problem text: change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students), remove the StudentCount class, and update the solution and any tests/examples accordingly. Also ensure the template/README hints expect an int. OR (B) Accept the wrapper type: update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount, document the StudentCount helper class and its API (e.g., getValue()), and provide a StudentCount template or explanation in the exercise text. Prefer option A (primitive int) to match the current UML and the exercise hint, unless the exercise intentionally teaches wrapper types — in that case choose B and update the problem text and template to avoid surprise.
